title: Bulkhead pattern — separate bounded pools per workload, no shared giant pool

s1_definition.profdef: The **bulkhead pattern** (named after ship compartments) isolates different workloads into SEPARATE, BOUNDED thread pools — each with its own core/max size, queue capacity, and rejection policy. If one workload's pool is exhausted (payment gateway down → all 20 threads blocked), OTHER workloads continue operating normally on their OWN pools. A single giant shared pool is wrong: one slow dependency exhausts the entire pool → ALL workloads fail (cascading failure). Bulkheads prevent this: payment pool full → payments fail gracefully (503). User pool, notification pool: unaffected. Each pool is independently monitored, sized, and tuned.
s1_definition.analogy: A ship has BULKHEAD WALLS dividing it into compartments. If one compartment floods, the walls contain the water — other compartments stay dry, ship stays afloat. Without bulkheads: one hole floods the ENTIRE ship → sinks. In banking: payment pool (20 threads), user pool (30 threads), notification pool (10 threads). Payment gateway down → 20 payment threads blocked. User requests and notifications: UNAFFECTED — their pools are separate. One giant 60-thread shared pool: payment gateway down → 60 threads consumed → EVERYTHING fails.
s1_definition.oneliner: Bulkhead = separate bounded pool per workload. One pool exhausted → only that workload fails. Others unaffected. Shared pool = single point of failure → cascading failure.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** The **bulkhead pattern** (named after ship compartments) isolates different workloads into SEPARATE, BOUNDED thread pools — each with its own core/max size, queue capacity, and rejection policy. If one workload's pool is exhausted (payment gateway down → all 20 threads blocked), OTHER workloads continue operating normally on their OWN pools. A single giant shared pool is wrong: one slow dependency exhausts the entire pool → ALL workloads fail (cascading failure). Bulkheads prevent this: payment pool full → payments fail gracefully (503). User pool, notification pool: unaffected. Each pool is independently monitored, sized, and tuned.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** A ship has BULKHEAD WALLS dividing it into compartments. If one compartment floods, the walls contain the water — other compartments stay dry, ship stays afloat. Without bulkheads: one hole floods the ENTIRE ship → sinks. In banking: payment pool (20 threads), user pool (30 threads), notification pool (10 threads). Payment gateway down → 20 payment threads blocked. User requests and notifications: UNAFFECTED — their pools are separate. One giant 60-thread shared pool: payment gateway down → 60 threads consumed → EVERYTHING fails.

**One line to remember:** Bulkhead = separate bounded pool per workload. One pool exhausted → only that workload fails. Others unaffected. Shared pool = single point of failure → cascading failure.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The banking platform had ONE shared 100-thread pool.** Payment gateway experienced a 30-second timeout event. 100 payment threads blocked for 30 seconds → pool exhausted. User login, balance inquiry, fund transfer — ALL queued behind blocked payment threads. 500 customers couldn't log in for 30 seconds because of a payment gateway issue. Fix: 3 bulkhead pools — paymentPool(20), userPool(50), notifyPool(10). Payment gateway timeout → only 20 threads affected → payment returns 503 → users still log in, check balance, transfer funds normally.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1 (shared pool — cascading).** Payment gateway timeout → 3 payment tasks block all 3 shared threads + queue full → user task submitted → RejectedExecutionException → user can't log in!

**Step 2 (bulkhead — isolated).** Payment gateway timeout → 3 payment threads blocked in paymentPool → paymentPool queue full → new payments rejected (503). userPool: 3 threads FREE → user profile loads instantly. Notification pool: 3 threads FREE → SMS sent normally.

**Step 3 (monitoring).** Each pool independently monitored: active count, queue size, completed tasks. Alert when paymentPool queue > 80% → "Payment gateway may be slow!"
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ SHARED POOL (WRONG — cascading failure) ═══

  sharedPool (60 threads):
  [pay][pay][pay]...[pay] × 60 ← ALL blocked on gateway!
  User request → REJECTED! Notification → REJECTED!
  EVERYTHING DOWN!

  ═══ BULKHEAD POOLS (CORRECT — isolated failure) ═══

  paymentPool (20):  [blocked][blocked]...[blocked] ← gateway down
                     → payments: 503 (Avoid) 
  userPool (30):     [working][working]...[idle]
                     → users: 200 OK (Recommended) (unaffected!)
  notifyPool (10):   [working][idle]...[idle]
                     → notifications: sent (Recommended) (unaffected!)

  One compartment floods → others stay dry!
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — Bulkhead Pool Configuration ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  ThreadPoolExecutor per workload          │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────────── │
  │  - corePoolSize: min workers (always on) │
  │  - maxPoolSize: burst capacity            │
  │  - keepAliveTime: idle thread timeout     │
  │  - workQueue: bounded! (LinkedBlockingQ)  │
  │  - threadFactory: named! (payment-1)      │
  │  - rejectionHandler: per-workload policy  │
  │                                            │
  │  Payment:  Abort (fail fast → 503)        │
  │  User:     CallerRuns (back-pressure)     │
  │  Notify:   DiscardOldest (drop stale)     │
  │  Batch:    CallerRuns (slow down producer)│
  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Resilience4j Bulkhead (alternative):
  BulkheadConfig config = BulkheadConfig.custom()
    .maxConcurrentCalls(20)
    .maxWaitDuration(Duration.ofMillis(500))
    .build();
  Bulkhead bulkhead = Bulkhead.of("payment", config);
  // Decorates: Supplier<T> decorated = Bulkhead.decorateSupplier(bulkhead, fn);
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The bulkhead pattern isolates different workloads into separate, bounded thread pools — each with its own size, queue capacity, and rejection policy. When one pool is exhausted (payment gateway down → all threads blocked), OTHER pools continue operating normally. A single giant shared pool is the WRONG design: one slow dependency exhausts the entire pool → ALL workloads fail (cascading failure). Named after ship bulkheads: one compartment floods, walls contain it, ship stays afloat.

Configuration per pool: core/max size based on expected load and IO characteristics. Bounded queue (not unbounded — prevents OOM). Rejection policy: AbortPolicy for critical paths (fail fast → 503), CallerRunsPolicy for back-pressure, DiscardOldestPolicy for non-critical notifications. Named threads for debugging (`payment-worker-3`). Monitoring: active count, queue size, rejection count per pool → Grafana dashboards + alerts. In banking: payment gateway timeout → shared 100-thread pool exhausted → 500 users couldn't log in. Bulkhead: paymentPool(20) exhausted → payments return 503. userPool(50): unaffected → users log in normally.

---

keyPoints: Separate pools per workload — isolate failures
One slow dependency does not consume all threads
